items.title: HUGE: OpenAI Raises Infrastructure Budget to $750 Billion
items.summary:
OpenAI has revised its cloud and computing budget upward to $750 billion through 2030 - a 25% increase from its earlier $600 billion projection, with a planned $30 billion data centre campus in Georgia requiring up to 3.2 gigawatts of power. 

In this episode of Front Page, we analyse the scale of OpenAI's revised infrastructure commitment, the strategic logic behind the Georgia data centre, and whether this front-loaded capital cycle represents a visionary land grab or an unsustainable spending spree.

items.title: EXPOSED: Humanoid Hype Is a $1.9 Billion Mistake - India Has Proof | Front Page
items.summary:
CYNLR's Cyro can grasp a completely unknown object in 10 to 15 seconds. Figure AI has raised $1.9 billion and is valued at $39 billion. The question is not which company has more capital - it is which one has understood the right problem.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Gokul, Founder of CYNLR, to break down why traditional robotic arms fail on factory floors, the baby brain principle behind CYNLR's CLX vision system, the collaboration with IISc Bangalore's Centre for Neuroscience, the fundamental flaw in Jensen Huang's physical AI scale thesis, Figure AI's safety lawsuit and the misallocation of capital in humanoid robotics, the vision versus imaging distinction that has held back the industry, CYNLR's Audi pilot involving mirror assembly across multiple unknown materials, the General Motors engagement across 22,000 parts, the case for sensing over actuation as the true source of robotic intelligence, and the path towards a universal shop floor that can be reprogrammed in software rather than rebuilt in steel.

CHAPTERS:
0:00 Introduction: Cyro vs Figure AI's $1.9 billion
1:21 Gokul's journey from 2007 to CYNLR
3:40 Why traditional robotic arms fail the factory floor
11:00 How robotic arms became a barrier to automation
13:03 The intelligence gap in current AI approaches to robotics
15:09 Baby brain principle and IISc Bangalore neuroscience
17:11 Vision vs imaging: the core misunderstanding in robotics
27:00 Sensing as the source of intelligence, not actuation
33:18 India's robotics ecosystem and the capital gap
37:34 Figure AI's safety lawsuit and capital misallocation
48:47 Why Jensen Huang's scale thesis won't solve manipulation
51:31 The universal shop floor: software-defined manufacturing
57:27 Audi pilot, General Motors and the path to deployment

items.title: Dentsu Global Services: Reimagining the GCC for an AI-Native Future
items.summary:
In this episode of the Simulated Reality podcast, we sit down with two special guests, Navin Dhananjaya, Global CXM Lead at Dentsu Global Services, and Vinay Mony, Senior Vice President, CXM at Dentsu Global Services.

Together, they explore how Dentsu Global Services is transforming from a traditional Global Capability Centre (GCC) into an AI-first intelligence hub. The conversation dives into building an AI-native workforce, scaling AI adoption across the organisation, creating secure governance frameworks, and delivering measurable business impact. They also discuss the future of customer experience, AI-powered research, intelligent automation, human-plus-AI collaboration, and why the next wave of enterprise innovation will be driven by organisations that successfully combine human expertise with AI to create real business value.
